subject: pharmacology
title: Drugs for shock and pulmonary arterial hypertension

steps.tx: **Shock** treatment begins by classifying the failure before any infusion starts in the emergency room. Vasodilatory shock needs vasoconstrictors, cardiogenic shock needs inotropes with pressure support, and hypovolaemic shock needs volume before drugs. Obstructive shock needs mechanical relief that no infusion can replace in a deteriorating patient. Teams then layer receptor targeted drugs with **source control** and fluids guided by responsiveness at the bedside. Lactate clearance, urine output, capillary refill and mentation judge success better than pressure numbers alone.
steps.say: Shock treatment begins by classifying the failure before any infusion starts in the emergency room today. Vasodilatory shock needs vasoconstrictors while cardiogenic shock needs inotropes with pressure support for the failing pump. Hypovolaemic shock needs volume before drugs and obstructive shock needs mechanical relief that infusions cannot replace ever. Teams judge success by perfusion markers because pressure numbers alone are misleading for clinicians at the bedside often. Source control decides survival more than any single vasoactive drug in most shock states treated.

steps.tx: **Vasopressin** constricts V1 receptors and works as a catecholamine sparing second pressor in septic shock. It may reduce atrial fibrillation compared with pure adrenergic escalation in critically ill patients on infusions. Terlipressin serves variceal bleeding and hepatorenal physiology in liver units with specialist supervision and monitoring. **Milrinone** increases contractility and dilates vessels for low output failure with raised pulmonary pressures in selected patients. That benefit costs hypotension and arrhythmias, and kidney failure prolongs its action considerably after stopping.
steps.say: Vasopressin is a vascular constrictor and it works as a second pressor in septic shock in intensive care. It may reduce atrial fibrillation compared with pure adrenergic escalation in critically ill patients receiving infusions concurrently over days. Terlipressin serves variceal bleeding and hepatorenal physiology in liver units with specialist supervision and careful monitoring provided. Milrinone increases contractility and dilates vessels for low output failure with raised pulmonary pressures in selected patients treated. That benefit costs hypotension and arrhythmias while kidney failure prolongs its action considerably after stopping therapy.

steps.tx: **Pulmonary arterial hypertension** is precapillary pulmonary vascular disease with three druggable pathways for targeted treatment. Endothelin antagonists block vasoconstriction, nitric oxide pathway drugs raise cyclic GMP signalling, and **prostacyclin** analogues replace a missing vasodilator. Combination therapy started early improves outcomes across most risk strata in modern specialist practice. Calcium blockers suit only the minority who show acute vasoreactivity during catheter testing in expert centres. Diuretics, oxygen, anticoagulation decisions and supervised rehabilitation complete the scaffold around drug therapy.
steps.say: Pulmonary arterial hypertension is precapillary pulmonary vascular disease with three druggable pathways for targeted treatment in specialists. Endothelin antagonists block vasoconstriction while nitric oxide drugs raise signalling inside pulmonary vessel walls in patients. Prostacyclin analogues replace a missing vasodilator and they improve exercise capacity in severe disease treated early. Combination therapy improves outcomes across most risk strata when specialists start treatment early in modern practice currently. Calcium blockers suit only the minority who show acute vasoreactivity during catheter testing in expert centres.

steps.tx: This arteriole section shows intimal fibrosis and medial thickening that narrow the lumen in **precapillary disease**. Three labelled pathways converge on the wall, where **endothelin** constricts through its receptors and bosentan blocks that signal. Nitric oxide raises cyclic GMP through soluble guanylate cyclase, and sildenafil protects that signal from breakdown by phosphodiesterase. Prostacyclin acts through its own receptor to raise cyclic AMP and dilate the vessel powerfully. Matching each drug to its labelled target turns this picture into a complete revision map.

steps.tx: In **right ventricular failure** the thin right ventricle needs adequate coronary perfusion pressure to keep contracting. Systemic pressure support therefore protects the right heart rather than threatening it in this setting. Careful preload matters because overfilling worsens **septal shift** and strangles left ventricular filling in a vicious cycle. Oxygen and correction of hypoxia, hypercapnia and acidosis reduce pulmonary afterload at the bedside quickly. Inhaled vasodilators unload the pulmonary circuit selectively without collapsing systemic pressure in critical care.

steps.tx: In **cardiogenic shock** after infarction, urgent revascularisation remains the definitive drug sparing therapy for survival. Noradrenaline restores pressure while dobutamine or milrinone improves flow from the failing pump in combination. Pure phenylephrine burdens a failing ventricle, dopamine provokes arrhythmias, and vasodilators alone collapse pressure dangerously in unstable patients. **Source control** decides survival more than any infusion label across every shock category in practice. Antibiotics, reperfusion, volume replacement or obstruction relief must accompany the infusion chart from the start.
steps.say: In cardiogenic shock after infarction urgent revascularisation remains the definitive therapy for survival in most patients presenting. Noradrenaline restores pressure while dobutamine improves flow from the failing pump in combination treatment given together promptly. Pure vasoconstriction burdens a failing ventricle and vasodilators alone collapse pressure dangerously in unstable patients treated aggressively without support. Cause treatment decides survival more than any infusion label across every shock category in clinical practice today always. Antibiotics, reperfusion, volume or obstruction relief must accompany the infusion chart from the very start indeed.
